title: 2. Entity relationship modelling and keys
description: Attribute classifications (derived, composite, multivalued), primary and foreign keys, candidate keys, cardinality, and referential integrity.

items.question: Which term describes a unique identifier that was not chosen as the primary key?
items.explanation: An alternate key uniquely identifies a record but is not the chosen primary key. It can still be used to look up the record.

references.label: Week 3 ER modelling, p. 6
references.file: reference/Oracle APEX/Week 3 - Entity Relationship Modelling 14 Oct 2026.pdf

items.question: An Address is broken into street name, postcode and city. What type of attribute is Address?
items.explanation: The slide uses Address as a composite attribute because it breaks down into components such as street name, postcode and city.

references.label: Week 3 ER modelling, p. 9

items.question: An employee’s pay is calculated from hours worked and wage information. What type of attribute is pay?
items.explanation: Pay is calculated from other attributes, such as hours worked and wage. That makes it derived.

references.label: Week 3 ER modelling, p. 9

items.question: A bookstore user may have no orders or place several orders; every order has exactly one user. What are the allowed counts for orders per user and users per order, respectively?
items.explanation: The bookstore allows a user to place zero, one or many orders, but each order must be placed by exactly one user.

items.question: What do the circle and crow’s foot at the ORDERS end mean?

options.text: Zero or many orders per user
An order can lack a user

items.explanation: Read the symbols at the Orders end from the User side: the circle allows zero and the crow’s foot allows many.

items.question: Which two columns form the composite primary key in the bookstore example?
items.explanation: The bookstore rule requires the combination of Order_ID and Book_ID to be unique, not either column by itself.

context.title: Bookstore order-item details
context.content: ORDER_ITEMS(Order_ID, Book_ID, Quantity, Price). Each row records one book on an order.

items.question: The library has one record for a book title and two physical copies of that title. Which foreign key should be added so that each copy points to its book title?

context.title: Mini Library — book titles and physical copies
rows: Each title has one or more physical copies.
One physical copy that can be borrowed
Each copy belongs to exactly one book title.

items.explanation: BOOK_TITLE is the one side and BOOK_COPY is the many side: one title can have several copies, but each copy belongs to exactly one title. So BOOK_COPY.BookID is the foreign key that references BOOK_TITLE.BookID. Each copy has its own CopyID as its primary key. For example, two copies of the same title have different CopyID values but share the same BookID.

references.label: Week 4 ERD practical: Mini Library, business rules BR3–BR5, p. 1
references.file: reference/Oracle APEX/Week 4 Practical ERD pt2 Oxt26.pdf

items.question: In the Mini Café, an order can contain several menu items, and the same menu item can appear on different orders. The café records how many units of each item were ordered on each order. In which table should the Quantity attribute be stored?
items.explanation: Quantity describes a particular menu item on a particular order, so it belongs in the Order–item junction table, which links orders to menu items. For example, one order may include two coffees and another may include one coffee. The menu item is the same, but the quantity differs by order. Storing Quantity in the Order table would not tell you how many units of each item were ordered.

references.label: Week 4 ERD practical: Mini Café Ordering System, p. 2
references.file: reference/Oracle APEX/Week 4 Practical ERD pt2 Oxt26.pdf
